records.title: RLUSD on the XRP Ledger: 99.6% of its payments were 110 bots
records.summary: Bitquery reports 7,821,066 account-to-account RLUSD payments from 19 September to 18 October 2026; 7,789,341 (99.6%) went from a cluster of 110 wallets to three collectors and carried only 7,722 RLUSD. The cluster received 13,341 RLUSD from Binance-labelled rDAE53 in 1,431 payments to 109 wallets and 5,419 XRP from six Binance-labelled wallets in 810 payments. It accounted for 1,580,084 of 3,467,989 account-to-account payments (45.6%) during 8–14 October and paid 495 XRP in fees for 8,602,917 transactions. After removing dust, Bitquery reports 14,600 payments of at least 1 RLUSD totaling $7.33B, 1,826 senders and 1,536 receivers; the ten largest senders moved $6.05B (82%), 828 payments of at least $1M moved $6.98B (95%), issuer mint/redemption plumbing moved $728M/$744M, and one wallet pair passed $424M each way. Bitquery explicitly says the pattern fits one Binance customer rather than Binance itself and that the Cross River shutdown timing does not establish causation.
records.limitations: Single analytics provider and one 30-day sample; the 110-wallet cluster is inferred from shared receivers and funding, not beneficial-owner identity. The detailed funding table says 109 wallets received RLUSD from rDAE53 although the cluster contains 110 wallets. Dust token authenticity was sampled from one sender for one day. Address labels may be incomplete. High-value transfer volume is gross ledger movement, not verified net external capital or economic settlement. The $424M roundtrip and issuer mint/redemption loop inflate gross volume. Bitquery states the bot shutdown coincided with the Cross River announcement but that no ledger evidence explains why.
